Bill Maher opens the floodgates when he asks, “Why?” James Talarico is a “very weird dude.”

Ted Cruz spends the next 2 full minutes going down the list.

Maher gives Talarico the benefit of the doubt until the “I really love trans children” quote drops.

Then he folds.

CRUZ: “I’m not going to convince you to love Ken Paxton. But you got to admit, Talarico, I think, is a very weird dude.”

MAHER: “Why?”

CRUZ: “Because he is like the ultimate woke social justice warrior. This is a guy who stands in front of a church... he says God is non-binary. He says there’s six genders. He stands in front of a church and says he weeps for his whiteness and weeps for his masculinity.”

MAHER: “That’s just weird. That is weird. I couldn’t agree with you more.”

KID ROCK: “Maybe he’s gay.”

MAHER: “What?”

KID ROCK: “Maybe he’s just gay.”

MAHER: “But why are we inferring — because he thinks Jesus is non-binary, which I don’t think he means as —”

[Kid Rock’s face isn’t buying a word of Maher’s explanation]

KID ROCK: “I know what he meant!”

MAHER: “What do you think he meant?”

KID ROCK: “Yeah, he’s trying to go into this whole ‘what’s a woman.’ Like, are we really talking about this 250 years later?”

MAHER: “No, I just think — look, I don’t know that much about it, but I have heard those quotes. I think what he meant by the Jesus is non-binary thing is that, you know, there are a lot of people who believe in God. I mean, your whole album is about Jesus, but in a more sort of ethereal way, more spiritual way. You know, he’s not the man in the sky with the beard, that kind of thing.”

CRUZ: “So Bill, all of these, he’s on video. He was asked, ‘Who do you really love?’ And his answer is, ‘Trans children.’ Well, I don’t know anyone else who would answer that question that way.”

MAHER: “Is that the full answer?”

CRUZ: “Yes, I promise you. You can pull up the video. He was asked, ‘Who do you really love?’ And he pauses and thinks and says, ‘I really love trans children.’ ... He also says on video that his objective is to, quote, ‘dismantle capitalism.’”

MAHER: “Look, I am not for any of that sh*t.”

CONTEXT: Talarico really did say it. On a 2023 podcast, he was asked what he loves other than family and friends, and his answer was the “trans children” who had rallied at the Texas Capitol the day before.

🇵🇱 Confused about WTF is going on in Poland? You're not alone

Yesterday, judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska took it upon herself to suspend the leadership of Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal

She issued written orders placing Tribunal President Bogdan Święczkowski and Vice-President Bartłomiej Sochański on a one-month “immediate break in official duties” and announced she was taking charge as the longest-serving judge

She justified this by arguing they had blocked newly elected judges from sitting, prevented the General Assembly from meeting (needed for the 2027 budget), and violated rules on assigning cases

The real reason is a spat over appointees to the court that President Nawrocki is refusing to accept. It's basically a fight over who controls the court - the left or right - with both sides claiming to act to make sure it's politically independent

I know, ironic, right

Her reasoning is that provisions in the 2016 Act on the Organization and Procedure before the Constitutional Tribunal state that the longest-serving judge can substitute for the President in certain situations when the President cannot designate a replacement

According to her, he cannot designate a replacement because she suspended him

She also claimed that Article 130 of the Law on the System of Common Courts permits a court president to order an immediate break in a judge’s duties for up to one month if the authority of the court or essential service interests require it (or if the judge is caught committing an intentional crime)

It's widely viewed as invalid because the Constitutional Tribunal has its own statute and is independent under the Constitution (Article 173) 

Ordinary-court rules on temporary suspension of presidents do not automatically transfer, and experts have called the claimed basis “non-existent” 

The Act on the Constitutional Tribunal does not provide for one judge unilaterally suspending the President this way

Korwin-Piotrowska herself is one of the judges elected by the current Sejm majority whose swearing-in President Nawrocki refused

The Justice Minister (who also serves as Prosecutor General) separately sought to lift the leaders’ immunity for prosecution, but he has no general supervisory power over the Tribunal the way he does over ordinary courts

The timing is wild too. She executed the move when President Nawrocki was on his way to Senegal

He turned his plane around mid-air, came back, and then had to force his way past a cordon of riot police to enter the Constitutional Court to try and resolve the chaos

Expect this one to get even more complicated and tense as both sides fight to exert control over Poland's highest court
